preface: This test is to confirm the POS automatically enters the Operator Break screen after the configured Auto Sign Off period of inactivity, printing no waybill.
preconds:
**GIVEN** an operator is signed on to the POS
**AND** the Auto Sign Off inactivity period is configured (use the configured value)
**AND** the POS is communicating with CloudFare
**AND** example: Operator → signed on, then left with no interaction

steps.content: **WHEN** the configured Auto Sign Off period elapses with no interaction
steps.expected:
**THEN** the POS goes to the Operator Break screen
**AND** no waybill is printed

steps.content: **WHEN** the CloudFare activity log is checked
steps.expected: **THEN** the corresponding event is recorded in the Back Office System (CloudFare) activity log

change_note: Corrected the outcome to match the resolved Break-mode model (Auto Sign Off inactivity timeout -> Operator Break, not straight to Idle; only continued inactivity on the Break screen -> suspend -> reboot). Previous wording asserted a direct sign-off to the Idle screen, contradicting the same fact already corrected on C4100360/C4100436 (same suite, cross-checked in batch_D).

preface: This test is to confirm power-cycling the POS for longer than the configured Auto Sign Off time forces a sign-off to the Idle screen, with no waybill printed, and records exactly one Forced Sign-off event.
preconds:
**GIVEN** an operator is signed on to the POS during a shift
**AND** the Auto Sign Off period is configured (use the configured value)
**AND** the POS is communicating with CloudFare
**AND** example: Operator → signed on, then the POS is powered off for longer than the configured Auto Sign Off time and back on

steps.content: **WHEN** the POS is power-cycled for longer than the configured Auto Sign Off time
steps.expected:
**THEN** on restart the POS returns to the Idle screen with no waybill printed
**AND** exactly one Forced Sign-off event is recorded to CloudFare

change_note: Added the outage-duration qualifier (longer than the configured Auto Sign Off time) and the no-waybill detail. A brief power interruption instead resumes the prior screen, and an outage shorter than Auto Sign Off resumes to Operator Break, not Idle (cross-checked against C4100360, same suite/batch_D) — the previous wording asserted an unconditional power-cycle-to-Idle outcome that only holds for long outages.
